previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: Mr. ___ was admitted with altered mental status and groin pain, found to be due to a urinary tract infection caused by pan-sensitive Pseudomonas aeruginosa, likely exacerbated by a missed indwelling catheter change. He was treated with intravenous piperacillin-tazobactam initially, then transitioned to oral ciprofloxacin after culture results. His mental status improved, consistent with resolution of metabolic encephalopathy. A right-sided varicocele was identified on scrotal ultrasound but deemed non-urgent with no evidence of mass effect on imaging. Left ankle erythema resolved and was attributed to bruising rather than cellulitis, leading to discontinuation of vancomycin. Hyperkalemia on admission normalized without intervention. He was discharged to extended care on a 12-day course of ciprofloxacin, with instructions to continue skin care and follow up with urology for his stable renal mass.

radiology_notes.text:
HISTORY:  Twitching and right upper extremity weakness.

TECHNIQUE:  Contiguous axial images were obtained through the brain without
intravenous contrast.

COMPARISON:  ___.

FINDINGS: Evaluation the skull-base is mildly limited due to motion artifact. 
Within this limitation, there is no acute intracranial hemorrhage, edema, mass
effect or major vascular territorial infarction.  The ventricles and sulci are
prominent compatible with age related atrophy.  Gray-white matter
differentiation is preserved aside from periventricular and subcortical white
matter hypodensities which likely reflect chronic small vessel ischemic
disease.  The left posterior fossa meningioma, which is partially calcified,
is unchanged.  There is no shift of normally midline structures.  There is no
fracture.  Imaged paranasal sinuses and mastoid air cells reveal a mucous
retention cyst or polyp in the right sphenoid sinus.

IMPRESSION: No acute intracranial process.
